posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Big number is a plugin that makes high numbers easier to read.
If variable 17 contain a large number, and you want to store an easier to read version in variable 18, you use the following plugin command:
Code:
bignumber 17 18
And the result will be:
This works for all numbers up to 999.99 decillion, and on request I can pump this number up even more.
Numbers:
Code:
<1000 = no change
                               1000 = thousand
                            1000000 = million
                         1000000000 = billion
                      1000000000000 = trillion
                   1000000000000000 = quadrillion
                1000000000000000000 = quintillion
             1000000000000000000000 = sextillion
          1000000000000000000000000 = septillion
       1000000000000000000000000000 = octillion
    1000000000000000000000000000000 = nonillion
 1000000000000000000000000000000000 = decillion
Download for
free

Big Numbers for MV by JohnDoeNews
This plugin makes big numbers up to 999 decillion easier to read

posts.author: VideoWizard
posts.body:
The limit is something like 1.79e+308 or thereabouts, about 179 uncentillion.
1e+303 is centillion, so you would need names from decillion (10-illion) to centillion (100-illion) Tredecillion is only 13-illion, so you have a ways!
Spoiler:
big, big numbers
Million, billion, trillion are known already, they're 1 followed by six, nine, and twelve zeroes respectively.
1e+15 = quadrillion (the 4th -illion)
1e+18 = quintillion
1e+21 = sextillion
1e+24 = septillion
1e+27 = octillion
1e+30 = nonillion
1e+33 = decillion (un, duo, tre, quattuor, quin, sex/se, septen, octo, novem)
1e+63 = vigintillion
1e+93 = trigintillion
1e+123 = quadragintillion
1e+153 = quinquagintillion
1e+183 = sexagintillion
1e+213 = septuagintillion
1e+243 = octogintillion
1e+273 = nonagintillion
1e+303 = centillion
1e+306 = uncentillion/cenuntillion, 179 of these is the max in 64-bit floating point, anything higher becomes positive infinity!
These are some big numbers!

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Huh? 12.590 would round to 12.60? I don't think so... 12.590 will always be shortened to 12.59, no matter if you round correctly or cut the number. 12.595 should round to 12.60
But to fixed doesn't round at all. It just guts away everything after. So basically it always rounds down. And I am fine with that, because otherwise when you need 1.24 million for something and you have 1.238 million, but it shows that you have 1.24 million (because it rounds up), that would seem like a bug. The game would say: you have the same amount as needed, but it isn't enough.
So I purposely cut the number, I don't round it. Rounding would be mathematically correct, but not a great thing in gameplay, if you ask me.
